content:
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price after a spike (e.g., +5%+ above mean); add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude as correction.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative; reduce first 5–7 days by 0.5–1.0%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 2σ above recent 30d mean, reduce by 10–15% of deviation; if < -2σ, increase by 10–15%.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from negative to positive) triggers 3–5 day lag correction: delay forecast peak by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 10–15%.
